sessionTitle: Data, apps, and agents: the future of app dev with Rayfin

announcements.name: Rayfin, the backend for the AI coding era
announcements.shortDescription: An SDK and CLI for authoring a full backend (database, functions, storage, access policies) in code, deployable to Fabric with one command for out-of-the-box enterprise security and compliance.
announcements.longDescription: Rayfin (heard as "Rayfind" [inferred]) is positioned as the backend for the AI coding era, providing an SDK and CLI that let a human and an agent define an entire backend in code—including the database, functions, storage, and access policies. Because everything is defined in code, both agents and humans can understand and operate it. When ready, you deploy with a single CLI command directly to Microsoft Fabric, where resources are provisioned and managed for you with enterprise-grade security and compliance out of the gate.

announcements.name: App as a new Fabric artifact type
announcements.shortDescription: Apps can be created directly from the Fabric portal via "new item," generating a deployed app artifact with a child SQL database in the workspace.
announcements.longDescription: From within the Fabric portal, a user can go to their workspace and click "new item" to find a new artifact type called "app." After naming it (e.g., an analysis app) and clicking create, you are given a choice of templates such as a blank app or a data app template that scaffolds the ability to query and connect to a semantic model with enterprise-grade visuals. The flow then continues in VS Code, where copying the template prompt and using Copilot's coding agent scaffolds the data app.

announcements.name: Data app template with Power BI
announcements.shortDescription: A template co-built with the Power BI team for building applications directly on the semantic layer, comprising a data package, a React/Vega-Lite visual package, and agent skills.
announcements.longDescription: The team partnered with the Power BI team to build a data app template, since one of the most common things enterprises build as data apps is dashboards. The template allows building applications directly on the semantic layer, so the effort invested in semantic models and the analytics stack can be reused for applications. It has three core components: a data package that normalizes the Fabric endpoint connection, query retries, and caching; a visual package using React and Vega-Lite components for flexible, AI-first visuals with enterprise-grade defaults; and agent skills that teach the coding agent how to use the packages effectively.

announcements.name: Connectors for existing Fabric data
announcements.shortDescription: Declarative connectors let apps read from and write back to databases, warehouses, and semantic models in OneLake, with agent instructions that pull schemas into typed classes.
announcements.longDescription: Rather than only spinning up a new backend and database, Rayfin introduces connectors that let apps connect to existing data in Fabric OneLake, including databases, warehouses, and semantic models, and—depending on the data source—write back to it. You declare the data source in your configuration, and agent instructions help pull in the relevant tables and generate classes so you get type safety. It selectively pulls only the schema you need (for example, a single table from a semantic model with hundreds of tables) rather than all the data. Related backend logic can be defined as functions in TypeScript that deploy as Fabric functions with rayfin up.

announcements.name: Replit partnership
announcements.shortDescription: Replit's browser-based agentic IDE can build and deploy apps into a Rayfin environment for non-technical users, announced on stage with Satya Nadella the prior day [inferred] and currently in private beta.
announcements.longDescription: Recognizing that not everyone works inside an IDE or CLI, the team announced a partnership with Replit, an agentic browser-based IDE where non-technical and semi-technical users can build apps. While Rayfin and Fabric target highly technical business users who want to get into the code, Replit serves users without coding experience who still want to build and deploy apps, inheriting the same enterprise-grade privacy and security properties. In the demo, a dashboard is built by giving the agent a Power BI semantic model, which it uses to generate the dashboard including underlying DAX queries, then deploys directly into a Rayfin environment.

announcements.name: Roadmap commitments
announcements.shortDescription: Upcoming support for functions, RBAC, additional OneLake and Blob storage connectors, OIDC and social login, real-time services, a perpetual free tier, and open-sourcing part of the Rayfin runtime for self-hosting.
announcements.longDescription: Wrapping up, the roadmap outlines what's coming after the current focus on core building blocks (database, enterprise auth out-of-the-box, and easy deployment to Fabric in a managed tenant). Very soon they will add support for functions, RBAC, and additional data connectors so you can connect to any data in OneLake and Blob storage. Looking toward the end of the year, they aim to support more B2B and B2C scenarios by moving beyond Entra auth to OIDC auth and real-time services, plus social login to get started without a company ID and a perpetual free tier. They also plan to open source part of the Rayfin runtime so applications can be self-hosted on various infrastructure.
